name: Boonaken
description: Boonaken is a lively Dutch Jass-family card game for 4-7 players, famously played for rounds of drinks. Its name is derived from the top three trumps: Boer (Jack), Nel (Nine), and Aas (Ace). It features a unique 'drinking game' structure where players strive to win twice to be safe, while losing twice results in buying the round. It combines standard Jass point-trick mechanics with a competitive auction and card exchange phase.

history.origins: Originating in the Dutch pub culture of the Hazerswoude-Rijndijk and Leimuiden areas, Boonaken is a social evolution of Pandoeren. It was specifically designed to find a single loser in a group to facilitate the purchase of drinks.
timeline: 19th Century: Jass games establish themselves across the Low Countries.
1950s: Boonaken emerges as a distinct pub variant in South Holland.
Present: Actively played in regional cafes; documented as a staple of local village social life.
history.cultural: Deeply tied to 'Café culture' in the Netherlands, where the social stakes (buying drinks) are as important as the card play itself.
history.evolution: The game streamlined the complex scoring of Klaverjassen into a simplified 'win/loss' tracker to maintain the fast pace required for a drinking game.

setup.players: 4 to 7 players playing individually (but forming temporary alliances against the declarer).
setup.deck: 32 cards (7, 8, 9, 10, J, Q, K, A in each suit).
setup.dealing: Deal 6 cards each. Center cards (widow) are dealt face-up or face-down depending on player count (e.g., 2 face-up for 5 players).
setup.equipment: Standard 32-card French pack, score sheet with +/- columns.

rules.objective: As declarer: Win your bid total in trick points + Roem. As defender: Stop the declarer. Overall: Win two rounds to be safe; avoid losing two rounds.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Auction**: Players bid point totals or special contracts (Misère, Zwabber). 2. **Exchange**: High bidder swaps cards with the center widow. 3. **Trump**: High bidder names the trump suit. 4. **Tricks**: 6 tricks played. **Must Follow Suit** rule is modified: you may trump even if you could follow suit. 5. **Roem**: Combinations (sequences/sets) announced at the first trick.
keyRules: Jass Trump Ranking: Jack (20), 9 (14), Ace (11), 10 (10), King (4), Queen (3), 8 (0), 7 (0).
Jack of Trumps can be withheld when trumps are led (Undertrumpping/Withholding).
Opponents can 'Counter-Roem' to cancel the declarer's bonus points.
Two '+' marks = Safe (exit game). Two '-' marks = Loser (buy drinks).

strategy.basic: Only bid for Declarer if you hold the Jack or Nine of trumps. The center cards are a gamble; don't rely on them to fix a void.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Trump Over' Maneuver: Use the rule allowing you to trump when you have the suit to steal high-point Tens or Aces from opponents early in the hand.
strategy.advanced: Roem Calculation: Precisely calculate your sequence values before bidding. If an opponent is likely to have a higher sequence, your bid may fail because your Roem will be cancelled.
tips: Wait for the right hand to bid Boonaak (all tricks) only when you control both the trumps and high side-suit cards.
In Misère (avoiding all tricks), use the withholding rule to dump your high trumps safely.

variations.name: Misère Bid
variations.description: A negative bid where the player must lose every trick. No trump suit.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This variation only changes the contract goal and does not yet require engine overrides.

variations.name: Zwabber
variations.description: The player must win every trick alone against all opponents.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This variation only changes the contract goal and does not yet require engine overrides.

scoring.description: 141 points in the pack. Declarer wins if trick points + uncancelled Roem ≥ bid. Win/loss tracking (not cumulative points).
scoring.winCondition: Avoid being the player with two losses.

synthesis.shortDescription: A fast Dutch Jass game for 4-7 players. Bid to win trick-points, exchange centre cards, announce Roem (card combinations) at the first trick, then battle through 6 tricks. Win twice and you're out safe. Lose twice? You buy the round. Named for the top three trumps: Boer-Nel-Aas.
